meta.appDescription: Your tracker tickets, worked by an AI dev team on this machine.

agentTime.definition: How long agents actually spent working, added up. Not how long the task took from start to finish — that mostly measures how quickly people replied.

acceptanceCriteria.definition: A short checklist of what must be true for the task to count as done. The team builds and tests against it.

agent.definition: An AI that does multi-step work on its own — reads your project, writes code, runs tests — instead of just answering a question.

apiKey.definition: A secret code that lets a program act on your account. Treat it like a password.

autopilot.definition: When switched on, the team approves plans, answers its own questions and works through the roadmap without waiting on you — inside a spend cap you set.

backlog.definition: The list of tasks waiting to be picked up.

branch.definition: A separate copy of the code where a change is made without touching the live version — until it is merged.

ci.definition: Continuous integration: automated checks that build and test every change, to catch problems before anyone sees them.

codeReview.definition: A second look at a proposed change before it is accepted — to catch mistakes and keep the code tidy.

commit.definition: A saved snapshot of code changes, with a short note about what was done.

deploy.definition: Publishing a new version of the app so people can use it.

diff.definition: A view of exactly what changed in the code — lines added in green, lines removed in red.

github.definition: The website where most of the world's code is stored and shared. Orkka can work on code that lives there.

lane.definition: A column on the board. Every task moves through the lanes, from idea to done.

mcp.definition: A standard that lets other AI tools — like Claude Code or Cursor — talk to Orkka directly.

merge.definition: Accepting a proposed change so it becomes part of the app.

milestone.definition: A meaningful chunk of the roadmap: a group of related tasks that together deliver something usable.

pipeline.definition: The steps every task goes through: plan, build, test, review, done.

plan.definition: The agent's step-by-step proposal for how it will do the task. Nothing is built until you approve it.

pr.definition: A proposed set of code changes, packaged so it can be reviewed before it becomes part of the app.

qa.definition: Quality assurance — testing the app to make sure it works as intended before anything goes out.

repo.definition: Where an app's code is kept, with a full history of every change — usually on GitHub. Think of it as the project's folder.

roadmap.definition: The ordered plan of what to build, grouped into milestones, that the team works through.

runner.definition: A small program you install on your own computer so agents work there, on your own AI subscriptions, instead of on Orkka's servers.

stack.definition: The set of technologies an app is built with — programming languages, frameworks, database.

tokens.definition: How AI models measure text — roughly three-quarters of a word each. AI provider plans count usage in tokens.

worktree.definition: A private working copy of the code for one task, so its changes stay separate until they are reviewed.

laneDrafting.definition: Where you write a task. Nothing happens to it until you move it to Ready.

laneReady.definition: Your PM picks the task up here — checks it is clear and complete, and asks you questions if not.

lanePlanning.definition: A developer agent is working out, step by step, how it will do the task.

lanePlanReady.definition: The plan is waiting for you. Approve it to start the work, or ask for changes.

lanePendingQuestions.definition: An agent needs something from you before it can continue. Answer in the task to get it moving again.

laneDeveloping.definition: The code is being written — in a private copy of the project, so nothing live is touched yet.

laneTesting.definition: Scout is trying the change in a real browser and checking it against the task's checklist.

laneCodeReview.definition: Sentinel is giving the change a second look. When it passes, the change is ready for you to approve.

laneDone.definition: Approved and part of the app.
